quests.question: The start-up hopes to _____ its relationship with the university to gain access to research and talented graduates.
quests.explanation: Using an existing connection to get extra benefits is the idea. To leverage something is to use it to maximum advantage.

quests.question: The software must be _____: it handles ten users today, but it has to cope with ten million later.
quests.explanation: Going from ten users to ten million requires the system to grow easily. Scalable means able to expand to handle greater demand.

quests.question: Could you _____ my application? My visa expires on Friday and I can't wait the usual three weeks.
quests.explanation: A tight deadline calls for speeding up the process. To expedite is to make something happen faster.

quests.question: Your job will be to _____ between the design team and the clients, making sure each knows what the other needs.
quests.explanation: Passing information between two groups is the role described. To liaise is to communicate and cooperate between parties.

quests.question: After the merger, two people were doing the same job, so one position was declared _____ and its holder lost her job.
quests.explanation: A role duplicated by another is no longer needed, which explains the job loss. In British English, a redundant job is one that is no longer necessary.

quests.question: We always keep a _____ plan in case our main supplier fails to deliver on time.
quests.explanation: A plan prepared for something going wrong is a backup. A contingency plan covers a possible future problem.

quests.question: The new reporting rules are so _____ that small shops spend more time on paperwork than on customers.
quests.explanation: Time lost to paperwork shows the rules are a heavy burden. Onerous means requiring great effort and causing difficulty.

quests.question: The company uses its biggest competitor's delivery times as a _____ for measuring its own performance.
quests.explanation: A standard used for comparison is a benchmark. It is a reference point against which things are measured.

quests.question: Before approving the plan, the council consulted all _____, including residents, shop owners and bus operators.
quests.explanation: These are all people affected by the decision. Stakeholders are people with an interest in or affected by a project.

quests.question: The new teacher quickly built a _____ with her class, and students felt comfortable asking questions.
quests.explanation: Students feeling at ease with her shows a good relationship. Rapport is a friendly understanding between people.

quests.question: All staff are expected to _____ to the safety guidelines at all times, without exception.
quests.explanation: 'Without exception' shows these are rules to be followed. To adhere to something is to follow it faithfully.

quests.question: A degree in engineering is a _____ for the role; without it, applications are not even considered.
quests.explanation: Applications without the degree are rejected, so it is required in advance. A prerequisite is something that must exist before something else.

quests.question: Rather than waiting for complaints, Leila is _____: she contacts clients before problems appear.
quests.explanation: Acting in advance instead of waiting is the opposite of responding after the event. Proactive means taking action before it is needed.

quests.question: 'Let's not worry about the venue yet; we'll cross that bridge when we come to it.' What does the speaker mean?
options: Deal with the problem if and when it actually happens
Ignore the problem completely and hope for the best
Plan carefully for every possible difficulty now
Ask someone else to solve the problem for them
quests.correctAnswer: Deal with the problem if and when it actually happens
quests.explanation: The speaker is postponing worry until the situation arises. The idiom refers to handling a difficulty only when it appears.

quests.question: After reviewing the data, the minister had to _____ that the policy had not worked as intended.
quests.explanation: Admitting something unwillingly after seeing the evidence is the idea. To concede is to admit that something is true, often reluctantly.

quests.question: Her English is _____; I have never found a single mistake in anything she has written.
quests.explanation: Not a single error means perfect standards. Impeccable means flawless.

quests.question: His _____ manner in meetings, constantly cutting people off and mocking their ideas, made colleagues avoid him.
quests.explanation: Interrupting and mocking create friction with others. Abrasive means harsh and rough in manner.

quests.question: To reduce risk, the farm decided to _____ and grow chillies and ginger as well as rice.
quests.explanation: Adding new crops to spread risk is the point. To diversify is to expand into different areas or products.

quests.question: After a _____ twelve-hour shift on her feet, Mira could barely climb the stairs.
quests.explanation: Being almost unable to climb stairs afterwards shows the shift was exhausting. Gruelling means extremely tiring and demanding.

quests.question: When Hugo began his reply with 'As I mentioned in my previous message,' Carla felt mildly criticised. What is the phrase implying?
options: She should already have read or remembered the information
He is thanking her for explaining it so clearly
He is changing the topic to something less awkward
He is apologising for not replying more quickly
quests.correctAnswer: She should already have read or remembered the information
quests.explanation: Pointing back to something already said suggests the reader missed it. The polite wording hides a small reproach.

quests.question: Share prices began to _____ as soon as news of the scandal broke, falling by thirty per cent in an hour.
quests.explanation: A thirty per cent fall in an hour shows a steep, sudden drop. To plummet is to fall quickly and dramatically.

quests.question: Attendance at the safety briefing is _____; anyone who misses it is not allowed on the site.
quests.explanation: Being barred for missing it shows it is compulsory. Mandatory means required by a rule.

quests.question: Granting one exception could set a dangerous _____: soon everyone will expect the same treatment.
quests.explanation: One decision that others will cite later creates a pattern to follow. A precedent is an earlier action used as an example for later ones.

quests.question: The treaty will take effect only when the parliaments of all member states formally _____ it.
quests.explanation: The treaty takes effect only after official approval. To ratify is to give formal consent to make something valid.

quests.question: The company's accounts have come under intense _____ since the fraud allegations.
quests.explanation: Fraud claims lead to close, critical examination. Scrutiny is careful and critical inspection.

quests.question: Nobody had considered the full _____ of moving the head office: lost staff, new rent costs, and a longer commute for everyone.
quests.explanation: The listed items are wide-ranging results of a single decision. Ramifications are the often complex consequences of an action.

quests.question: The laptop I received was _____: the screen flickered and the keyboard stopped responding after two days.
quests.explanation: A faulty screen and keyboard show the product doesn't work properly. Defective means having a fault.

quests.question: He tried to _____ himself with the director by laughing at every one of her jokes and offering to carry her bags.
quests.explanation: Flattering behaviour to win favour is the clue. To ingratiate yourself is to try to gain someone's approval, usually by flattery.

quests.question: Her results were _____: she exceeded every target and achieved the highest score of any trainee that year.
quests.explanation: Beating every target and topping the cohort is exceptional performance. Outstanding means far better than average.

quests.question: After ten years in politics, he felt _____, no longer believing that he could change anything.
quests.explanation: Losing faith in what he once hoped for is the key. Disillusioned means disappointed on discovering that something is less good than believed.
